title: Audit-ready security brief: SIEM export & RBAC evidence checklist
body:
Purpose:
This document is a concise, customer-facing brief for responding to vendor security questionnaires and auditor requests that focus on RBAC v2, audit log schema, and SIEM export/evidence automation. The goal is to give a compact set of answers, a reproducible evidence export procedure, and an index of artifacts we typically provide to auditors.

Audience:
- CS/solutions engineering when preparing responses for SOC2, ISO or procurement questionnaires
- Security reviewers at customer organizations and their external auditors
- Internal on-call and SREs who need to produce evidence quickly

Topline answers (short snippets to paste into questionnaires):
1) RBAC model and least privilege: 
   - Redwood implements a role-based access control (RBAC v2) system with explicit role definitions, resource-scoped permissions, and attribute-based constraints for cross-tenant operations. Roles are mapped to a minimal set of CRUD actions and segregated by scope (global, org, project, resource). Service accounts and API keys are constrained by role and optionally bounded by time-to-live (TTL).

2) Audit logging and integrity: 
   - All access and configuration changes are recorded in an immutable append-only audit log with RFC3339 timestamps. Logs include request metadata (request_id, actor_id, actor_type, tenant_id), resource identifiers, pre/post config diffs where applicable, action name, outcome (success/failure), IP and user agent, and server-side correlation ids. Logs are signed at rest and stored redundantly for the customer retention period.

3) SIEM export: 
   - We support streaming and batch export of audit events to customer SIEM endpoints (syslog/CEF/JSON over HTTPS) and provide a time-bounded export bundle (ndjson) for audits. Exported fields follow a stable schema (see Audit Log Schema section below).

Quick RBAC v2 mapping (one-paragraph explanation for auditors):
RBAC v2 centralizes authorization via a role service. Roles contain permission sets (verbs) scoped to resource types (e.g., models, deployments, keys). Role bindings associate principals (user, group, service-account) with scope (org, project). We enforce deny-by-default and validate role transitive grants at bind-time; cross-tenant privileges require explicit elevation and are logged with an elevation ticket. Admin role grants are subject to MFA and privileged access approval workflows.

Audit Log Schema (canonical fields we expose to customers):
- timestamp: RFC3339 UTC
- request_id: internal UUID (correlation across services)
- tenant_id: opaque customer org id
- actor_id: user or service account id
- actor_type: user | service | system | automation
- actor_roles: comma-separated active roles at time of action
- action: canonical action name (e.g., deployment.create, model.access, policy.update)
- resource_type: e.g., deployment, model, key, route
- resource_id: opaque resource identifier
- outcome: success | failure | denied
- ip: originating IP address (if available)
- user_agent: client UA string
- request_payload_sha256: SHA256 of request payload when stored for audit (if applicable)
- response_code: HTTP style numeric code for the action (where applicable)
- pre_change: base64-encoded JSON diff (optional, for config changes)
- post_change: base64-encoded JSON diff (optional)
- retention_policy: retention label attached to event
- export_batch_id: identifier for exported bundles

NOTE: For SIEM exports we flatten nested fields to dot notation (actor.roles => actor_roles) and produce NDJSON where each line is a single event.

Sample SIEM export command (internal):
- One-off export to NDJSON for auditors: 
  1) Request export via internal tooling: `ops-evidence-export --tenant <TENANT> --from 2024-07-01 --to 2024-09-30 --format ndjson --include pre_change,post_change --output s3://evidence-bucket/<TENANT>/audits/2024Q3/`
  2) Verify checksum: `sha256sum <file> > <file>.sha256` and sign using internal keyring (artifact stored in metadata).
  3) Create access artifact and share URL with auditor (tempo-limited pre-signed S3 URL) and include manifest.json that lists file names, checksums, and job id.

Automation playbook (how to produce an evidence bundle quickly):
1) Use the `ops-evidence-export` service (runbook available in Confluence).
2) Input: tenant id, time range, desired schema (ndjson/json/cef), optional filters (actions, resources).
3) The tool validates parameters, starts a job, streams events into compressed ndjson, computes per-file SHA256, and writes manifest.json (job metadata: start, end, exporter id, retention tag, s3 path).
4) Security reviewer verifies artifact integrity by comparing manifest checksums and verifying the job id in our audit log (audit job events are themselves logged).

Evidence checklist (what we usually provide to customers/auditors):
- Exported NDJSON audit log(s) covering requested period
- manifest.json with job id, checksums, and exporter metadata
- RBAC role definitions snapshot (roles.json) with timestamps
- Role bindings snapshot (bindings.json) showing principal->scope mappings
- Sample policy evaluation logs (for deny/allow decisions) where requested
- System architecture diagram showing where logs are generated and exported (PDF)
- SLA and retention policy excerpt (PDF)
- Redaction summary if any PII was redacted as part of export (log of redaction events)

Handling common customer questionnaire items (suggested copy):
Q: How do you demonstrate least privilege?
A: We provide role definitions and binding snapshots, plus a time-bounded list of admin elevation events. Role definitions are immutable once versioned; changes create a new role version and produce an audit event.

Q: Can we get raw logs for a third-party audit?
A: Yes — we deliver signed NDJSON bundles and an integrity manifest. For live integrations we can configure real-time forwarding to your SIEM via HTTPS or syslog.

Q: How long do you retain logs?
A: Default retention is 90 days for hosted customers; enterprise customers can request custom retention via contract and we store per-tenant retention metadata. Retention labels are present on each exported event.

Operational notes and gotchas (internal tips for engineers/SEs):
- Preflight: ensure the requested time range is covered by the customer's retention policy before promising exports.
- Redaction: exports will redact customer-provided secrets by default; include a redaction summary if redaction applied.
- Correlation: ask for request_ids or time windows when customers ask for specific incidents — this speeds up exports.
- Cost: large exports (multiple TBs) may require pre-approval — quote to customer if needed.
- SIEM mapping: customers who use CEF often want different field names; we support a CEF adapter but require a mapping ticket to ensure legal and privacy checks.

Minimal scriptable example (NDJSON line example):
{"timestamp":"2024-08-21T19:12:03Z","request_id":"b6a8c3f2-...","tenant_id":"org-7b2","actor_id":"user-92","actor_type":"user","actor_roles":"developer,model-reader","action":"model.access","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"m-1234","outcome":"success","ip":"18.204.7.23","user_agent":"redwood-sdk/1.4.0","response_code":200} 

Redaction & privacy: 
- We redact PII in request/response payloads by default unless a customer signs a narrow exception. Redaction decisions are logged and included in the manifest (redaction events with reasons).

When to escalate to security: 
- Customer requests full non-redacted request/response payloads
- Export requested for time ranges outside retention without contractual agreement
- Suspicion of tampering or checksum mismatch during verification

Deliverables template (what SEs should attach to customer message):
- Signed manifest.json (contains job id and checksums)
- Link to signed NDJSON bundle (pre-signed URL)
- Snapshot of roles.json + bindings.json (timestamped)
- Short explanation note (one page PDF) describing scope and redaction policy applied

Notes / open items (WIP):
- Add a standard RBAC diff tool output so auditors can see what changed between role versions (priority: Q4).
- Template Acceptance Criteria for export SLAs (time to produce large export) — need sales/legal input.
- Consider a canned SIEM connector for Splunk/QRadar to reduce custom mapping tickets.

References and deep links: 
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Evidence+Export
- RBAC design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC-v2-Design
- Ops export repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-evidence-export

Contact and escalation: 
- Primary: Sofia Chen (security)
- Backup: Priya Nair (product-security)
- If auditor/legal require an NDA or extra legal review, route to Legal via internal intake form (link in Confluence).

Version history:
- 2024-10-10 Sofia Chen: initial draft
- 2024-11-02 Ethan Rivera: added operational checklist and sample NDJSON line

This brief is intentionally short and copy-friendly. Use the short answers above for questionnaire fields and attach the artifacts listed in the deliverables template when sharing with auditors. For any non-standard requests route to product-security for approval and scheduling.
